CD4+ lymphocyte dysfunction, as measured by the loss of the ability of CD4+ lymphocytes to express the cytokine IFN-gamma, is associated with the progressive course of SIV disease and that effective vaccines, which control SIV replication, can prevent this CD4+ lymphocytic dysfunction.
the capacity of CD4 T lymphocytes to produce cytokines is impaired during the course of simian immunodeficient virus infection and that vaccination prevents this impairment.
CD4+ lymphocytes from monkeys with stable clinical status express more cytokine than CD4+ T cells from monkeys with AIDS, and that vaccination prevents the CD4+ T cell dysfunction.

the mechanisms of CD4+T lymphocyte dysfunction in simian immunodefiency virus (SIV) infection and the ability to prevent this process by vaccination.

the present studies provide evidence for a role for CD4+ T-cell dysfunction in the development of AIDS in a primate model and that effective vaccines may be protective.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CD4 T cells from SIV-infected rhesus monkeys that control virus replication and have preserved T cell counts have a preserved cytokine expression capacity, whereas CD4 T cells in SIV-infected animals that have progressed to AIDS have a dysfunctional cytokine expression capacity.
CD4 T lymphocytes from simian immunodeficieny virus-infected monkeys have a global loss of cytokine expression.

vaccination can prevent CD4+ T-cell dysfunction.
